name: Strength Workout Log
description: Record your own exercises, actual sets and loads, compare history, and save personal routines
help: Records use ToolForge’s existing local database. No connection is required after installation.
Create your exercises in Exercises & routines, then start a workout and confirm each actual set.
Copied sets and routines begin as pending input. Only completed sets contribute to totals.
History is retained without count-based trimming. Lists are paginated; review an actual date or an exercise.
A complete backup contains one JSON volume per workout. Keep and restore every volume from the same batch. Existing unrelated records are never silently replaced.

exercise.title: My exercises
exercise.hint: Keep equipment and variations separate, even when names match. Past workouts keep their original snapshots.
exercise.name: Exercise name
exercise.snapshotHint: Changes apply to newly added exercises. Existing workouts and routines keep their original tracking mode.
exercise.archiveHint: Archived exercises leave the add menu. Past workouts and routines stay intact, and exercises can be restored.

workout.title: Current workout
workout.name: Workout name
workout.empty: Add your exercises to this workout
workout.emptyHint: You enter the actual repetitions and load. No training program is generated.
workout.welcomeHint: Create a new workout or reopen a draft below.
workout.reviewHint: {{count}} sets are still pending. They remain in the record but are excluded from completed totals.

rest.hint: A rest cue for this page. Reopening shows elapsed status and never adds workout records.

history.title: Workout history
history.hint: Paginated in creation order. Choose an actual date to review that day. Equipment and variations remain separate; original load and kilograms are shown together.

template.title: Personal routines
template.name: Routine name
template.hint: Build a routine from these exercises and set inputs. All copied sets start pending in a new workout.
template.createHint: Arrange exercises and enter your own target sets in a workout, then save it as a routine. No training program is generated.
template.deleteHint: This only deletes the routine. Existing workouts and actual records remain.

backup.title: Export and restore
backup.restored: Volumes restored; you can continue importing this batch
backup.hint: Save a complete backup to a folder: one JSON volume per workout, with exercises and routines included. History has no automatic retention cap. Keep every volume from a batch. Individual workouts can also be exported as CSV.
backup.export: Back up everything to a folder
backup.importHint: Choose all JSON files from one backup batch. Restore into an empty journal or continue the same batch; unrelated data is never replaced. Repeated volumes are skipped. Retry after a partial failure.
backup.privacy: Records stay on this device. Backups contain personal workout notes; keep them somewhere safe.

errors.workout.invalid: An input or saved record is invalid. Check names, dates, repetitions and load.
errors.workout.version: This data version is unsupported. Existing data has not been replaced.
errors.workout.incompleteSet: Enter actual repetitions before completion, and actual load for externally loaded exercises.
errors.workout.duplicateExercise: This exercise is already present. Add another set instead.
errors.workout.limit: A workout supports 64 exercises and 100 sets per exercise. Reduce this workout.
errors.workout.documentLimit: This individual record is too large. Reduce long notes or this workout; history is never automatically deleted.
errors.workout.noUndo: There is no set action to undo.
errors.workout.importConflict: This backup belongs to another journal. Existing data has been kept.
errors.workout.readLimit: Related records could not be loaded. Retry; existing data is unchanged.

volume.summary: List completed sets as text and get the set count, total reps, volume (kg) and heaviest load
volume.sets: Each set as "repsxweight[kg|lb]", e.g. 8x60kg; reps alone for bodyweight; comma separated or repeated
volume.unit: Weight unit used when a set has none
